title: Math formulas, level 3: identities and rules
trouble: Rereading feels like knowing; it is not. Recall, then check.

blocks.html: Identities are statements that are true for every value of the letters. They are the tools for simplifying and solving in algebra, trigonometry and beyond, and they show up on every high school and college entrance test.

How to hold it: Each rule has a reason you can check with small numbers: try a = 3 and b = 2 in (a + b)² and see why the middle term 2ab must be there. Checking with numbers is retrieval practice and proof at once. Chunk by family (special products, exponents, trigonometry, logarithms), and notice that the log rules are the exponent rules in disguise.
This list has 15 items. Answer below, then check — the practice button generates fresh questions from the list itself.
